description: We  are STEM students united by a shared passion for space exploration and Earth science. We combine our diverse skills in science, technology, engineering, and math to analyze our home planet from a unique vantage point.
summary:
We developed EARTHFLIP — One Planet. Different Stories., an interactive climate exploration platform that investigates how air temperature changes across different regions of the world.

Its core innovation is the Opposite Trend Detection Engine, which analyzes temperature trends across 12 selected regions worldwide, including two locations in Egypt, and identifies statistically significant increasing and decreasing trends.

EARTHFLIP addresses NASA's Space Apps Challenge, "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!", by allowing users to investigate environmental changes, compare regional patterns, and discover contrasting temperature trends.

The project is important because global averages can hide significant regional differences. EARTHFLIP makes climate data more accessible and helps users understand that different parts of our planet can experience different temperature changes.
details:
EARTHFLIP — One Planet. Different Stories.

EARTHFLIP is an interactive climate data platform designed to explore how temperature trends differ across regions of the world. Instead of looking only at global average temperatures, it allows users to investigate 12 selected locations, including two in Egypt, and discover regions experiencing significantly different temperature trends.

Users can select a time period and explore monthly air temperature data from NASA's POWER database. The platform processes the data and applies statistical methods, including the Seasonal Mann-Kendall test, Sen's slope estimator, and Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate correction, to identify statistically significant increasing and decreasing trends. Its main feature, the Opposite Trend Detection Engine, compares regions with opposite trend directions and makes these differences easier to explore.

The project helps make complex climate data more accessible and understandable. It highlights how climate change does not affect every region in the same way, encourages users to investigate regional patterns, and demonstrates why looking beyond global averages is important. Including two Egyptian locations also connects the global analysis to local environmental conditions.

What makes EARTHFLIP creative is its focus on comparing different climate stories rather than simply presenting temperature charts or a single global trend. It combines data exploration, statistical analysis, and interactive visualizations in one platform.

The project was developed using Python, with FastAPI and Uvicorn for the backend, NumPy and Pandas for data processing, SciPy for statistical calculations, Requests for accessing NASA POWER data, and SQLite for local data caching. The frontend provides the interactive interface and visualizations. No additional hardware was required.

During development, we considered data availability, the length of the historical record, data completeness, statistical significance, and the importance of comparing geographically different regions. We also considered accessibility and clarity so users can explore the results without needing advanced knowledge of climate science.
